note: ILLUSTRATIVE DEMO FIXTURE prepared by the Field Verse SE team. NOT ML predictions or agronomic recommendations. Indicator ratings are illustrative 1–5 values chosen by people from general crop knowledge.
limitations: Demo strategies were prepared by hand for a typical rain-fed maize field near Njoro; they are not calculated for your exact field.
No market prices, seed availability or labour data were used.
Soil values (when shown) come from a global estimate (SoilGrids), not a soil test of your field.

strategies.name: Maize each long rains (current)
strategies.summary: One maize crop in the long rains every year, with the land mostly unused for the rest of the year.

steps.notes: Field left after harvest; crop residues may remain.

reasons: This is a common pattern in the area.

indicators.label: Water needed
indicators.explanation: One rain-fed crop timed with the main rains.

indicators.label: Soil cover through the year
indicators.explanation: The field is uncovered for about half the year.

indicators.label: Exposure to dry spells
indicators.explanation: A poor long-rains season affects the only crop of the year.

indicators.label: Range of products to sell
indicators.explanation: One product. No price data was used.

notes: NASA POWER shows the long rains peak around April, supporting a main-season crop.
Uncovered from about September to February.

benefits.text: Familiar crop with known markets and methods.
Maize is a staple food for many households.

risks.text: Growing maize after maize can build up pests and diseases and use up soil nitrogen.
All income depends on one crop in one season.

explanation.summary: This is your current pattern, shown as the starting point for comparison.
details: Rainfall data shows a second, smaller rainy period in October–November that this pattern does not use.
explanation.technical: Baseline strategy. Indicator ratings are illustrative demo values.

dataGaps.text: No soil test of your field is available.
Local pest and disease history is unknown.

localChecks: Ask your extension officer about maize disease pressure in your area.

uncertainty.notes: Illustrative demo content; no model has evaluated this field.

strategies.name: Maize – Common bean
strategies.summary: Maize in the long rains, then common beans in the short rains.

reasons: The short rains (October–December) can support a short bean crop.

indicators.label: Water needed
indicators.explanation: Both crops are rain-fed and timed with the rainy seasons.

indicators.label: Soil cover through the year
indicators.explanation: Field is covered for most of the year.

indicators.label: Natural nitrogen added
indicators.explanation: Beans are legumes and may add some nitrogen.

indicators.label: Exposure to dry spells
indicators.explanation: Beans are sensitive to drought if the short rains fail.

indicators.label: Range of products to sell
indicators.explanation: Two products. No price data was used.

notes: October–November average about 115–145 mm of rain per month (NASA POWER).

benefits.text: Uses the short rains that the current pattern leaves unused.
Beans may add nitrogen for the next maize crop.
Beans are a nutritious food crop and a second product to sell.

risks.text: Beans are sensitive to drought; a weak short-rains season can reduce yields.
Maize harvest must finish in time for bean planting in October.

explanation.summary: This option adds a bean crop in the second rainy season, making more use of the land and the rain.
details: NASA POWER shows a second rainy period in October–November.
Bean varieties of about 70–110 days could fit into that window.
explanation.technical: Illustrative demo strategy. Indicator ratings are hand-prepared, not model outputs.

dataGaps.text: Your maize variety's harvest date (affects bean planting time).

localChecks: Ask which bean varieties are recommended for short rains at your altitude.
Check your maize variety's maturity time.

uncertainty.notes: Illustrative demo content; short-rains reliability varies between years.

strategies.name: Maize – Lablab cover
strategies.summary: Maize in the long rains, followed by lablab to cover the soil and provide fodder.

steps.notes: Deep roots can keep it growing into the dry months.

reasons: Cool temperatures at this altitude may slow lablab growth.

indicators.label: Water needed
indicators.explanation: Lablab is known for coping with dry periods.

indicators.label: Range of products to sell
indicators.explanation: Fodder for livestock or beans for food. No price data used.

notes: Can use September–November rain and continue into January.
Continuous cover can protect soil from erosion.

benefits.text: Protects soil for most of the year.

risks.text: Mean temperatures here are only about 14–17 °C (NASA POWER); lablab may grow slowly in the cool highlands.
A vigorous vine can be hard to manage before the next maize planting.

explanation.summary: This option focuses on protecting and feeding the soil, with fodder as a bonus.
details: The cool highland climate is the main uncertainty, so this option is marked for review.
explanation.technical: Illustrative demo strategy. Feasibility flagged because observed mean temperatures are low for a warm-season legume.

dataGaps.text: How lablab performs at your exact altitude.

localChecks: Ask farmers nearby or the extension office whether lablab grows well at your altitude.

uncertainty.notes: Illustrative demo content; highland performance is uncertain.
